Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States  Mixed  Fed on hold / tariff fog
🇪🇺 European Union  Bullish  ECB on hold / recovery
🇨🇳 China  Mixed  targeted easing / weak credit
🇯🇵 Japan  Bullish  hike bias / weak yen
🇦🇺 Australia  Bearish  hiking bias / sticky inflation
🇵🇱 Poland  Bullish  easing cycle / strong growth
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Beats are table stakes; guidance and capital return get paid
🔍 Underowned Themes — Active on X, Underweight in Portfolios
Large-cap software after the AI scare — Microsoft
Short squeeze off the lows; stablecoins are the growth story
Duration bid, dollar steady, credit cracks in private markets
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
The Fed's March call — labour data decide
$NVDA  beat-and-raise into the Vera Rubin ramp  ↑
Tesla / TSLA  "retail buys what institutions sell"
body: Thursday, February 26 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The US mix is slower growth with sticky inflation, which keeps the Fed parked. Fourth-quarter GDP rose at a 1.4% rate, badly missing estimates, while inflation firmed to 3% CNBC [Feb 20]. January payrolls rose 130,000, beating forecasts, and unemployment fell to 4.3% CNBC [Feb 11]; Governor Waller says the March rate call depends on the labour market Bloomberg.com [Feb 23], so there is no near-term cut while jobs hold. AI earnings are strong, but macro is not delivering the rate relief multiples were counting on.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.45% and the 10Y at 4.05%, a 10Y−2Y spread of +60 bps; over 20 observations the 2Y fell 8 bps and the 10Y 19 bps, a bull flattening (both down, 10Y down more) that took 11 bps off the spread (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25). The curve is positively sloped and approaching, but still below, its long-run average, and bond traders see Fed cuts spilling into 2027 Bloomberg.com [Feb 25], so the long end has done the rallying. The S&P 500 closed at 6,946.13, down 0.47% over 20 sessions, with the VIX at 17.93 and the DXY at 97.70 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

New / Most Important: Trade policy, not the Fed, is the new shock. The Supreme Court ruling against Trump's tariffs is unlikely to end the trade-policy chaos AP News [Feb 24]: a replacement global tariff started at 10% and the administration is working to lift it to 15% Reuters [Feb 24]. The path matters more than the level — uncertainty delays capex outside AI and keeps foreign investors questioning their US weight, while possible refunds are a one-off windfall for importers.

Playbook ✓: Own 5Y–10Y duration (IEF) while the 10Y stays below its 4.24% level of 20 observations ago (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25): sub-2% growth caps long yields even with the Fed on hold CNBC [Feb 20]. Overweight the AI-capex chain and industrials, underweight consumer discretionary. What changes the call: a firm next payrolls print plus hotter inflation that lifts the 2Y back above 3.53% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25) — then cut duration and add banks.

Macro Stance: Europe has the better macro mix. Eurostat confirmed euro-area inflation at 1.7% in January Eunews [Feb 25], leaving the ECB an easing option rather than a hiking risk, and European shares closed at a record high on an HSBC boost and easing AI-disruption fears Reuters [Feb 25]. The STOXX 600 finished at 633.47, up 4.1% over 20 sessions, against a 0.47% fall for the S&P 500 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

Activity & Inflation: February's PMI showed euro-zone businesses performing better than expected as manufacturing bounced back Reuters [Feb 20]; with inflation at 1.7% Eunews [Feb 25], that is a disinflationary recovery, the best mix for equity multiples. EUR/USD closed at 1.1775, down 2.02% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), easing pressure on exporters. The risk is that the factory bounce is restocking ahead of US tariffs rather than final demand.

New / Most Important: ECB leadership is now a market variable: economists expect Lagarde to exit early and hand the job to Knot Bloomberg.com [Feb 25], which markets would likely read as less dovish at the margin — more relevant for periphery spreads than for the rate path. The US tariff reset to 10% with a push toward 15% Reuters [Feb 24] keeps EU-US trade in limbo, with autos and luxury most exposed to any retaliation.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight European equities versus the US, led by banks with wealth franchises and utilities, funded from US discretionary; the Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,173.32 is up 4.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). What changes the call: EU retaliation against US tariffs, a PMI that gives back February's rebound Reuters [Feb 20], or a succession fight that widens periphery spreads.

Macro Stance: China is a consumer bounce layered on a still-deflating credit and property base, so we stay Mixed: tactically constructive on consumption and onshore equities, cautious on anything that needs credit growth. Tourism spending over the Lunar New Year hit a record $116 billion Caixin Global [Feb 25], a genuine demand signal. But one holiday does not repair household balance sheets hit by falling home prices, and the policy response so far is targeted rather than broad.

PMIs & Activity: The latest official read is January's manufacturing PMI, which dropped to 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30], still in contraction. The February PMIs are the next print, and the feed carries no fresh activity data beyond holiday spending Caixin Global [Feb 25]. A manufacturing reading back above 50 would confirm that the consumption pulse is broadening into production; a second sub-50 print would mark the holiday boost as a one-off. Our base case is a services-led stabilisation with manufacturing hovering near 50, which favours consumer names over industrials.

Credit Impulse: January new loans jumped but missed forecasts as weak demand persisted Reuters [Feb 13], so the impulse reflects seasonal front-loading rather than a demand revival. Beijing is leaning on targeted measures such as city-level property relief Bloomberg.com [Feb 24] rather than broad stimulus, and the yuan's strength gives it room to do more. Without stronger household borrowing the credit impulse stays flat; what would change that is a February loan print that beats on household medium- and long-term loans, which the feed does not yet carry.

Property: New home prices extended their decline in January as weak demand hounded the sector Reuters [Feb 12]. Shanghai eased homebuying rules in the latest round of property relief Bloomberg.com [Feb 24]; easing in the largest tier-one market matters symbolically, but local relief has not yet stopped price declines, so we treat it as floor-building rather than a turn. Confirmation would be two consecutive months of narrowing new-home price falls, and until then developers and property-heavy banks stay underweight.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: The US tariff regime was reset after the Supreme Court ruling AP News [Feb 24]: a new global tariff started at 10%, with a push to 15% Reuters [Feb 24]. To the extent the new rate applies uniformly, it narrows China's relative penalty, a relative win for Chinese exporters. Industrial policy is aimed squarely at technology — China targets a five-fold increase in advanced chip output to meet AI demand Nikkei Asia [Feb 25]. The feed carries no new central fiscal stimulus figure; a consumption-support package building on the record holiday spending Caixin Global [Feb 25] is what would move us to Bullish.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite closed at 4,147.23, up 0.82% over 20 sessions, and ASHR at 34.57 is up 2.37%, while the Hang Seng sits at 26,765.72, up 0.06%, KWEB at 32.24 is down 10.19% and FXI is down 3.81% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). USD/CNY closed at 6.8831, down 1.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), with the yuan near a three-year high as US dollar uncertainty grows South China Morning Post [Feb 25]. The split is clear: the onshore market and the currency are being bought, offshore internet platforms are being sold.

New / Most Important: The yuan is the story. Its move to near a three-year high South China Morning Post [Feb 25] loosens domestic financial conditions, lifts the dollar value of onshore earnings for foreign holders and gives the PBOC room to ease without currency pressure. The tech push is the second leg: the planned five-fold expansion in advanced chip output Nikkei Asia [Feb 25] targets exactly the AI bottleneck that has driven global semis. That argues for owning onshore hardware and equipment suppliers and for treating foreign chip-tool vendors' China revenue as a multi-year risk.

Playbook ✓: Own the onshore leg through ASHR rather than KWEB — ASHR is up 2.37% over 20 sessions while KWEB is down 10.19% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — and keep a modest long-CNY position while USD/CNY trends lower. Avoid mainland developers until new-home price declines narrow Reuters [Feb 12]. Upgrade to Bullish on a February manufacturing PMI above 50 plus a loan beat; downgrade to Bearish if Beijing retaliates against the new US tariff. ⚠ Divergence: traders are piling into bearish yuan bets to hedge downside risks Bloomberg.com [Feb 25] even as spot sits near a three-year high — the options market does not trust the rally.

Macro Stance: Japan is the cleanest reflation trade in developed markets: record equities, a weak yen and a central bank still leaning toward tightening. Governor Ueda flagged a chance of a rate hike in March or April in a Yomiuri interview Reuters [Feb 25]. The political counterweight is real — in a surprise move the government tapped two reflationists for the BOJ board Reuters [Feb 24] — but that slows the pace of hikes rather than stopping them.

Activity & Currency: USD/JPY closed at 155.88, up 2.25% over 20 sessions, and the Nikkei 225 at 58,583.12, up 10.77% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The weak yen is doing more for equities than domestic growth: Q4 GDP grew an annualised 0.2%, below expectations Nikkei Asia [Feb 16]. The reflationist board picks Reuters [Feb 24] pushed the yen lower again, flattering exporters' earnings but testing the BOJ's tolerance.

Playbook ✓: Stay long Japanese equities, tilted to exporters and banks: a weak yen lifts translated earnings, and a March or April hike Reuters [Feb 25] widens bank margins. Hedge half the currency exposure. What changes the call: USD/JPY pushing well above 155.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) into intervention territory, which would trigger a sharp yen squeeze and an exporter sell-off, or the BOJ skipping both meetings as the new board members dilute the hawks.

Macro Stance: Australia is the developed market where the next policy move is still up. January's core inflation hit a 16-month high, raising bets on a May rate hike Reuters [Feb 24]. Governor Bullock says she does not think inflation is taking off again ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Feb 25], but with core inflation still rising, households face the risk of higher mortgage costs into mid-year — a headwind for domestic demand and rate-sensitive equities.

Demand & Financing: AUD/USD closed at 0.7061, up 0.93% over 20 sessions, and the S&P/ASX 200 at 9,128.30, up 2.18% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Corporate Australia is cutting labour costs: WiseTech plans to slash 2,000 jobs as AI ends the era of manually writing code ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation [Feb 25]. Job cuts at a software leader alongside sticky core inflation is a stagflation-lite mix for domestic demand, and we expect resources and banks rather than rate-sensitive sectors to carry the index.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive domestic cyclicals and A-REITs; express Australia through the AUD and resources instead, where a strong currency and a firm RBA reinforce each other. Trigger to turn Mixed: a softer next monthly CPI that takes the May hike Reuters [Feb 24] off the table. Risk to the AUD long: a US-Iran escalation that hits global risk appetite.

Monetary & Activity: Poland pairs fast growth with on-target inflation. GDP growth accelerated to 4% (PKB przyspieszył do 4 procent — 'GDP accelerated to 4 percent') Bankier.pl [Feb 12], and January CPI landed in the target band, though above forecasts, with economists assessing the chances of a March rate cut (inflacja w celu, ale powyżej prognoz — 'inflation on target, but above forecasts') Money.pl [Feb 13]. The risk is that the upside surprise persuades the RPP to pause.

FX & Markets: EUR/PLN closed at 4.2139 and USD/PLN at 3.5790, up 2.48% over 20 sessions on dollar strength (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). EPOL rose 2.0% to 38.71 in the prior session and the Beta ETF WIG20TR closed at 69.17, up 2.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Leaders: KGHM at 342.00, up 13.17% over five sessions, plus Orlen (PKN) at 115.10 and Pekao (PEO) at 233.40, up 9.66% and 7.86% over 20 sessions; CD Projekt at 249.00 is down 12.82% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

Companies: Orlen plans to inject 5.1 billion zlotys into utility unit Energa Reuters [Feb 25], strengthening the group's grid and generation investment capacity. KGHM is the market's lever on copper, which closed at 5.98, up 2.59% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — the purest Polish exposure to the AI data-centre and grid metal. PKO at 93.58 and PZU at 69.90 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) anchor the dividend trade alongside Pekao.

Security & New Development: Poland, Germany, France, Italy and the UK will jointly develop low-cost air-defence systems Notes From Poland [Feb 23], which keeps defence and engineering order books full. The bill is fiscal: the European Commission warns Poland's debt is on track to breach 100% of GDP by 2036 Euronews [Feb 25]. That caps how far Polish government bonds can rally even as the RPP eases, and it makes the zloty more sensitive to any fiscal slippage headline.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Poland via EPOL or the WIG20TR ETF, with PKO, Pekao and KGHM as core holdings; add on a March rate cut that leaves the zloty stable. What changes the call: a hawkish RPP hold, EUR/PLN breaking sharply higher, or fiscal slippage. ⚠ Divergence: house prices recorded their first annual fall since 2013 Notes From Poland [Feb 24] — a turning property cycle sits awkwardly with a bank-led equity rally.

Narrative: Consensus spent February pricing an 'AI scare' against software: XLK is down 3.4% over 20 sessions and MSFT 16.64% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is whether AI partners with incumbents or replaces them; Nvidia's Jensen Huang says markets 'got it wrong' on the threat to software CNBC [Feb 25].

Reported: Salesforce beat and committed $50 billion to buybacks CNBC [Feb 25], while Workday hit a more-than-five-year low as a sluggish sales forecast sparked AI-disruption fears Reuters [Feb 25]. The market's test is the forward subscription guide, not the quarter.

EPS Upside Watch: Hardware and chip-design software tied to AI build-outs: Nvidia's earnings and guidance beat, with data-centre revenue up 75% CNBC [Feb 25], feeds straight into server and networking demand. Seat-based software is where expectations are lowest, so in-line guides can now surprise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The contrarian trade is the crowded short in large-cap software: if Huang is right CNBC [Feb 25], MSFT at 400.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) prices disruption that has not reached its numbers, while Workday's slide Reuters [Feb 25] shows the risk is real for narrow, seat-based vendors rather than platforms.

Narrative: Communication services are flat: XLC is down 0.34% over 20 sessions, META closed at 653.69 and GOOGL is down 6.47% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is capex versus ad returns — Meta struck an AI chip deal with AMD days after committing to deploy millions of Nvidia GPUs CNBC [Feb 24].

Reported: The Trade Desk slid after earnings as its growth slowdown unnerved Wall Street MarketWatch [Feb 25], a warning for programmatic ad spend outside the walled gardens. Netflix rose 5.97% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Platforms with their own AI inference capacity should keep taking ad budgets from independent ad-tech MarketWatch [Feb 25]; Meta has estimate upside if second-sourcing chips from AMD CNBC [Feb 24] lowers its compute cost per ad dollar.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Consensus treats Big Tech capex purely as a cost; multi-vendor chip deals show the largest buyers gaining pricing power over suppliers — a margin positive that is not in estimates, so we would not short the platforms on capex headlines alone.

Narrative: Financials are split between strong bank earnings and a private-credit scare: XLF is down 2.13% over 20 sessions, though BAC rose 2.54% and JPM 2.02% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Bloomberg reports private-credit fears deepening with a UBS warning of 15% defaults Bloomberg.com [Feb 25].

Reported: HSBC was the reporting standout, lifting European shares to a record close Reuters [Feb 25]; in the US the sector is trading private-credit headlines rather than fresh earnings Bloomberg.com [Feb 25].

EPS Upside Watch: Money-centre banks with trading and wealth franchises: volatility and capital-markets activity support fees even as a flatter curve trims margins. GS at 921.38 rose 2.12% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The contrarian signal is geographic: HSBC's results drove European shares to a record Reuters [Feb 25] while US financials trail. Global banks with wealth franchises are re-rating and US alternative managers and BDCs are de-rating — own the former, avoid the latter until private-credit marks settle.

Narrative: Energy is the year's leadership trade: XLE is up 10.47% over 20 sessions, Brent closed at 70.85 and WTI at 65.42 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is the Iran risk premium — Trump set a 10–15 day deadline for a deal or 'bad things' Reuters [Feb 20].

Reported: EOG beat profit estimates on strong output and higher gas prices Reuters [Feb 24]; XOM at 149.06 and CVX at 184.22 are up 8.94% and 8.97% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Upstream oil producers carry the most estimate upside if Brent holds, because consensus was built on lower prices; gas-weighted names are the exception, with Henry Hub at 2.97, down 57.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Supply is loosening under the geopolitics: OPEC+ is considering a 137,000 bpd output increase for April Reuters [Feb 25]. An Iran deal would leave rising supply and no premium — hold the sector with Brent puts.

Narrative: Industrials are the AI-capex beneficiary with real earnings: XLI is up 6.39% over 20 sessions, CAT 19.99% and GE 15.27% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Consensus is right on direction but too narrow — the demand story is broadening from data centres into construction and farm equipment.

Reported: Deere boosted its outlook and sees construction and small-agriculture demand recovering WSJ [Feb 19]; Axon jumped 17% after results Livemint [Feb 25]. Both were rewarded for lifting forward guidance, not merely beating.

EPS Upside Watch: Machinery and power equipment: Deere's recovery call WSJ [Feb 19] suggests the agriculture and construction cycle is bottoming on top of data-centre power demand. CAT at 766.61 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) is the cleanest combination of both, and its estimates still embed a flat construction cycle.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Aerospace is not participating: BA at 230.36 is down 5.81% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) while machinery leads. The industrial upswing is a capex story, not a travel or defence-prime story, so pair longs in machinery against aerospace underweights.

Narrative: Discretionary is the weakest cyclical: XLY is down 4.56% over 20 sessions and AMZN 13.91% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is a cautious middle- and lower-income consumer, compounded by AI-capex fatigue at the sector's largest weight.

Reported: Home Depot topped estimates for the first time in a year but said project demand remains muted CNBC [Feb 24]; Lowe's dipped 4.2% despite its beat Livemint [Feb 25]; TJX forecast muted annual sales and profit as consumers curb spending Reuters [Feb 25]. Housing-linked retail is being priced on volumes, not beats.

EPS Upside Watch: Home improvement on a lag: US mortgage rates reached their lowest since 2022, boosting refinancing Bloomberg.com [Feb 25], and refinancing tends to fund home projects with a delay. HD at 375.57 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) is the name to own first if housing turnover confirms.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Retail is buying what institutions sell in Tesla Yahoo Finance [Feb 22], which keeps TSLA at 417.40, down only 3.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), while the rest of discretionary de-rates — the sector's largest single-stock risk now sits with retail holders.

Narrative: Staples are the crowded defensive: XLP is up 7.03% over 20 sessions and WMT 7.53% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), and 24/7 Wall St. counts consumer staples up almost 20% while the S&P 500 struggles 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 25]. The rally is rotation into safety, not an earnings upgrade cycle.

Reported: Diageo fell nearly 13% after slashing its dividend and lowering its profit outlook CNBC [Feb 25] — the defensive label does not protect against volume declines. COST slipped 0.37% in the prior session to 994.76 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Scale value retailers — Walmart, Costco — have the cleanest estimate path, but after a near-20% sector rally 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 25] the upside is in the price. Branded food, beverages and spirits face negative revisions as volumes weaken and promotions rise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Novo Nordisk plans to halve the US list price of Wegovy from 2027 Reuters [Feb 24]; cheaper GLP-1 drugs widen the volume threat to snack and beverage makers just as their multiples peak. Defensive money is crowding into the part of staples most exposed to that shift.

Narrative: Healthcare is a policy story: XLV is up 1.53% over 20 sessions while LLY closed at 1,028.83, down 1.03% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). CMS Administrator Oz says most-favoured-nation drug pricing will become the standard CNBC [Feb 25], which caps pharma multiples.

Reported: Pharma reporting in the feed window was thin; the sector's defining announcement was Novo Nordisk's plan to halve the US list price of Wegovy from 2027 Reuters [Feb 24]. That moves the obesity category from volume-led growth toward price competition.

EPS Upside Watch: Managed care rather than pharma: MFN pricing CNBC [Feb 25] shifts economics away from manufacturers and toward payers. UNH rose 3.74% in the prior session to 284.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), and lower drug list prices reduce benefit-cost pressure into the next guide.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The obesity franchise is turning into a price war: list-price cuts Reuters [Feb 24] put pressure on the category leader, and LLY is down 1.03% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) despite its dominance. Growth investors still treat GLP-1s as a duopoly volume story; the pricing data say otherwise.

Narrative: Materials are a metals trade: XLB is up 6.16% over 20 sessions, gold closed at 5,226.20 and copper at 5.98, up 2.59% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). J.P. Morgan sees gold at $6,300 by the end of 2026 Reuters [Feb 25].

Reported: Rio Tinto reported record copper and bauxite production for 2025 Yahoo Finance [Feb 23] — copper is now the growth engine for diversified miners. FCX at 68.82 is up 9.46% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Copper producers, as owners of the AI data-centre and grid metal: record output at Rio Yahoo Finance [Feb 23] and firm prices point to upward revisions for FCX and KGHM-type pure plays. Gold miners lag bullion — NEM is down 1.69% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — leaving margin upside if prices hold.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Silver is the warning: SLV is down 21.21% over 20 sessions despite a 14.2% five-session rebound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), a reminder that precious-metal momentum can reverse violently even with a $6,300 gold call on the table Reuters [Feb 25].

Narrative: Real estate is benefiting from falling long yields: XLRE is up 5.31% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), and CNBC reports that dividend-paying real estate stocks are outperforming as AI fears roil markets CNBC [Feb 23].

Reported: REIT reporting in the feed window was light; the sector is trading rates, with the 10Y down 19 bps over 20 observations to 4.05% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25). XLRE closed at 43.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Residential and housing-adjacent REITs: mortgage rates at their lowest since 2022 Bloomberg.com [Feb 25] should lift transaction volumes and lower refinancing risk for leveraged landlords, which feeds funds-from-operations estimates with a lag.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Real estate is behaving as an AI hedge rather than a pure rate play CNBC [Feb 23]: investors are buying physical cash flows that software cannot disrupt. That bid can persist even if yields stop falling, which makes the sector more resilient than its rate beta suggests.

Narrative: Utilities are the AI-power trade: XLU is up 9.05% over 20 sessions and CEG 12.84% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Trump says he has told big tech companies to build their own power plants Reuters [Feb 25], putting generation at the centre of the AI build-out.

Reported: Constellation topped earnings estimates Investor's Business Daily [Feb 24] and rose 10.81% over five sessions, while VST closed at 175.36, up 6.76% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

EPS Upside Watch: Independent power producers with nuclear and gas fleets — CEG, VST — can sign direct supply deals with hyperscalers if behind-the-meter power becomes policy Reuters [Feb 25]. NEE at 95.11, up 9.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), offers the renewables leg.

⚡ Breaking Convention: 'Bring your own power' cuts both ways: if hyperscalers self-supply, regulated utilities lose some of the load growth that justified their capex plans. The trade therefore favours generators over wires-and-pipes utilities, a split the sector ETF hides.

Narrative: European autos are a value trap: the STOXX autos tracker closed at 46.15, down 0.85% over five sessions, and VOW3 at 99.94 is down 4.0% over the same span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The driver is weak European demand and the cost of the EV transition Automotive News [Feb 23].

Reported: New car registrations fell 3.9% in January, with battery-electric cars at a 19.3% share ACEA - European Automobile Manufacturers' Association [Feb 24], and Stellantis faces its first annual loss after EV write-downs Automotive News [Feb 23].

EPS Upside Watch: Upside is scarce; the least-bad estimate path is at the premium end — BMW at 88.12 and Mercedes at 58.99 are up 1.29% and 2.75% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — but neither has a volume catalyst while registrations fall ACEA - European Automobile Manufacturers' Association [Feb 24].

⚡ Breaking Convention: Stellantis is the contrarian: STLA at 7.71 is down 20.92% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), so the write-down risk Automotive News [Feb 23] is largely priced and any sign of a US sales recovery would meet very low expectations.

Narrative: Semis remain the AI earnings engine: SOXX is up 4.82% over 20 sessions, TSM 14.6% and ASML 4.94%, while AMD is down 16.34% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The memory boom is the new layer, leaving PC and smartphone makers in the cold Financial Times [Feb 25].

Reported: Nvidia beat on earnings and guidance, with data-centre revenue up 75% CNBC [Feb 25]; TSMC raised its dividend 28% on 38% revenue growth 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 25]. Both confirm that AI demand is still accelerating at the foundry and accelerator level.

EPS Upside Watch: Memory and foundry: MU at 429.00 is up 4.57% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) with pricing power from the memory squeeze Financial Times [Feb 25], and TSMC's dividend increase 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 25] signals management confidence in sustained AI demand.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The losers sit inside tech: memory costs are a margin hit for PC and handset makers Financial Times [Feb 25], so the AI chip boom is a transfer from device makers to chipmakers rather than a tide that lifts all hardware. Pair chip longs with device-maker underweights.

Rewarded: Companies that paired a beat with a raised outlook or visible demand: Axon jumped 17% Livemint [Feb 25], Deere boosted its outlook WSJ [Feb 19], Constellation topped estimates Investor's Business Daily [Feb 24], and HSBC's results lifted European shares to a record Reuters [Feb 25]. Nvidia's earnings-and-guidance beat CNBC [Feb 25] extended the pattern into the AI supply chain.

Punished: Beats with soft guides were sold: Workday hit a five-year low on a sluggish sales forecast Reuters [Feb 25], Lowe's dipped 4.2% and GoDaddy slumped 16% Livemint [Feb 25], TJX's muted forecast weighed Reuters [Feb 25], and Diageo fell nearly 13% after cutting its dividend CNBC [Feb 25].

Pattern: The market pays for forward visibility and penalises two things: subscription models seen as exposed to AI substitution, and consumer companies guiding cautiously. Hard-asset and AI-infrastructure exposure is rewarded even at high valuations, while optically cheap consumer and software names keep de-rating on in-line numbers.

Attention into EPS: Attention shifts to the AI-infrastructure tail of the season: CoreWeave, where options traders expect a 15% move on its Q4 results tastylive [Feb 24]. Nvidia's forecast of accelerating growth CNBC [Feb 25] raises the bar for every AI-supply-chain report that follows, because in-line guides will now read as deceleration.

Playbook: Buy beats only with raised guides; fade beats paired with flat outlooks on the first bounce. Into prints, prefer companies with buyback capacity — Salesforce committed $50 billion CNBC [Feb 25] — and physical AI exposure over seat-based software. Change the call if two or more software names rally on in-line guides, which would signal the de-rating is exhausted.

Attention Gap: Morgan Stanley calls Microsoft the most under-owned stock 24/7 Wall St. [Feb 18], and MSFT is down 16.64% over 20 sessions to 400.60 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The AI-disruption narrative has been applied to the whole software complex, yet Huang argues the market got that threat wrong CNBC [Feb 25], and platform vendors own the distribution that AI agents need.

Exposure & Risk: Express through MSFT shares or a software ETF such as IGV, adding in stages and only after the stock stops making lower lows. Risks: new AI-agent launches that reignite the rout, Workday-style guidance misses spreading to larger vendors Reuters [Feb 25], and capex intensity weighing on free cash flow.

Attention Gap: US mortgage rates are at their lowest since 2022 and refinancing is picking up Bloomberg.com [Feb 25], but attention is on AI and the market still treats housing as frozen — Home Depot says project demand remains muted CNBC [Feb 24]. The 10Y is down 19 bps over 20 observations to 4.05% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25), which feeds into mortgage pricing with a lag.

Exposure & Risk: Express via HD at 375.57, down 1.26% over 20 sessions, and XLRE at 43.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), plus homebuilder ETFs such as ITB and XHB. Risks: a tariff- or oil-driven rebound in yields that closes the window, and households using refinancing savings to repair balance sheets rather than spend.

Market Context: Bitcoin closed at 67,960.12, up 6.06% on the prior completed daily close and 8.39% over 20 days, while ether rose 10.88% to 2,054.63 and solana 11.23% to 87.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). Equity proxies outran spot: COIN rose 13.52%, MSTR 8.86% and IBIT 7.39% in the prior session, though IBIT is still down 22.52% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

New / Most Important: The fundamental news is in stablecoins, not tokens: Circle reported $770 million of Q4 revenue with USDC circulation reaching $75 billion The Block [Feb 25]. Even after the bounce, bitcoin is heading for its worst month since the crypto collapse of June 2022 Bloomberg.com [Feb 24], so the market is separating payment rails, which are growing, from speculative assets, which are still deleveraging.

Playbook: Treat bitcoin's rally as a squeeze until it clears the hurdle around $70,000 that CoinDesk flags CoinDesk [Feb 25]; above it, add spot or IBIT, and below the 20-day low cut risk. Prefer stablecoin rails — Circle, Coinbase — over spot beta, given USDC growth The Block [Feb 25]. What changes the call: renewed ETF outflows or a risk-off shock from Iran.

Rates & Dollar: The DXY closed at 97.70, up 1.54% over 20 sessions but flat over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), so the dollar has stabilised rather than broken lower. The long end is bid: TLT is up 2.4% and IEF 1.42% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), consistent with a 10Y at 4.05% and a bull flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25). BofA says US stocks drew their lowest share of global flows since 2020 Bloomberg.com [Feb 20].

Credit Check: Public credit is calm: HYG closed at 80.92, down 0.31% over 20 sessions, and LQD at 111.65, up 0.76% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The stress is private — Bloomberg reports a UBS warning of 15% defaults Bloomberg.com [Feb 25] — and it has not yet reached high-yield ETF prices. We read that as complacency rather than resilience: tight public spreads leave no cushion for a private-credit spill-over.

Portfolio Implication: Keep credit beta low: prefer LQD over HYG and avoid listed BDCs and alternative managers until private-credit marks settle. Own IEF/TLT as the hedge against an AI-capex or private-credit accident, and fund international overweights — Europe, Japan, Poland — from US discretionary, in line with the global flow rotation Bloomberg.com [Feb 20]. Change the call if HYG breaks lower on rising defaults or a strong payrolls print lifts the 2Y back toward 3.53% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25).

What Is Priced: The US issued new Iran sanctions on the eve of nuclear talks in Geneva Al Jazeera [Feb 25], after Trump set a 10–15 day deadline for a deal Reuters [Feb 20]. Oil carries a premium — Brent closed at 70.85, up 4.85% over 20 sessions, and gold at 5,226.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — but the VIX at 17.93 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) says equities price a contained outcome.

Conditional Expression: If talks produce a framework, fade the premium: trim XLE, sell Brent upside and buy airlines and European cyclicals. If talks fail and strikes follow, own Brent call spreads, XLE and gold, and underweight airlines, oil-importing emerging markets and carry trades funded in low-yielders that suffer in risk-off.

Risk: The binary is not clean. OPEC+ is considering a 137,000 bpd increase for April Reuters [Feb 25], so a deal could push oil below pre-tension levels quickly, while a limited strike could spike prices only briefly. Size positions for a gap, not a trend, and prefer options to outright futures.

What Is Priced: Bond traders have pushed expected Fed cuts into 2027 Bloomberg.com [Feb 25], and Waller says the March decision depends on the labour market Bloomberg.com [Feb 23]. The 2Y at 3.45% is only 8 bps lower over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-25), so a March cut is not the base case.

Conditional Expression: If the next payrolls report disappoints, the 2Y has the most room to fall: own 2Y notes or a 2s10s steepener and add small caps — IWM closed at 264.58, down 0.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). If payrolls beat again after January's 130,000 CNBC [Feb 11], expect the 2Y to reprice higher and the dollar to firm; favour banks and energy over duration.

Risk: Inflation, not jobs, could decide: fourth-quarter inflation firmed to 3% CNBC [Feb 20], and tariff pass-through could keep the Fed on hold even with softer hiring. A hold with soft data would flatten the curve further and hurt small caps.

Catalyst & Thesis: Nvidia's results beat on earnings and guidance, with data-centre revenue up 75% CNBC [Feb 25], and its forecast points to accelerating growth as Vera Rubin starts hitting the market CNBC [Feb 25]. Our thesis: supply, not demand, is the binding constraint into the Rubin ramp, which supports pricing and margins through the year and keeps hyperscaler capex flowing to Nvidia first.

Price Hurdle & Risk: NVDA closed at 195.56 before the report, up 1.41% on the day and 3.73% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). The hurdle is holding above that pre-report close: a beat-and-raise that cannot hold the level would say investors are fading AI capex regardless of results. Bullish while above 195.56; the call fails on a close back below it within a few sessions or on any sign hyperscalers are trimming orders.

Catalyst & Thesis: CoreWeave's Q4 results are the next AI-infrastructure test, with options traders pricing a 15% move tastylive [Feb 24]. Our thesis: the reaction will hinge on funding costs and capex, not revenue, because the private-credit market that finances GPU fleets is under stress, with UBS warning of 15% defaults Bloomberg.com [Feb 25]. A revenue beat paired with higher interest expense would be sold.

Price Hurdle & Risk: CRWV is not on our market card, so no level is quoted. The risk to the short is Nvidia's accelerating guide CNBC [Feb 25], which implies scarce GPU capacity and pricing power for neoclouds; cover on faster backlog conversion with lower funding costs.

Catalyst & Thesis: Constellation topped earnings estimates Investor's Business Daily [Feb 24], and the next catalyst is policy: Big Tech companies are to meet Trump at the White House to sign a pledge on data-centre power costs CNBC [Feb 25] after he told them to build their own power plants Reuters [Feb 25]. Nuclear fleets that can contract directly with hyperscalers are the cleanest beneficiaries of that shift.

Price Hurdle & Risk: CEG closed at 325.84, up 4.22% in the prior session, 10.81% over five sessions and 12.84% over 20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25). After that run, add only on pullbacks that hold the post-results gap; the call fails if the pledge shifts grid costs onto generators or if hyperscalers favour new gas builds over existing nuclear.

Observed Attention: Goldman Sachs lists Strategy and Coinbase among the most-shorted stocks Yahoo Finance [Feb 25]. MSTR rose 8.86% in the prior session to 135.65 but is down 16.05% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

Motivation & Bias: Retail is playing for a squeeze: heavy short interest plus a bitcoin bounce is a classic setup. The bias is to treat short interest as fuel rather than as a hedge against bitcoin exposure, and the stock amplifies bitcoin in both directions.

Instrument & Risk: Prefer defined-risk call spreads to shares or leveraged single-stock ETFs; the trade works only if bitcoin clears the $70,000 hurdle CoinDesk [Feb 25]. Risk: bitcoin is still on track for its worst month since June 2022 Bloomberg.com [Feb 24].

Observed Attention: Retail investors are piling into Tesla as institutional investors sell Yahoo Finance [Feb 22]. TSLA closed at 417.40, up 1.96% in the prior session and down 3.13% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

Motivation & Bias: Loyalty and the autonomy narrative: retail treats institutional selling as a buying opportunity, a contrarian bias that works in squeezes but ignores fundamentals such as falling European car registrations ACEA - European Automobile Manufacturers' Association [Feb 24].

Instrument & Risk: Prefer shares or long-dated calls over daily-reset leveraged ETFs in a choppy tape. Risk: if institutions keep distributing, retail becomes the marginal buyer at ever-higher conviction and thinner liquidity.

Observed Attention: Reddit's silver bears 'waved the white flag' as SLV climbed Yahoo Finance [Feb 24]; SLV rose 14.2% over five sessions to 80.04 and silver futures closed at 90.94 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25).

Motivation & Bias: Momentum chasing after a crash: a short-covering rally is being read as a new uptrend, with gold's strength and a $6,300 J.P. Morgan gold target Reuters [Feb 25] used as validation.

Instrument & Risk: Use SLV with a stop rather than leveraged silver products; SLV is still down 21.21% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25), so this is a rebound inside a downtrend. Risk: a US-Iran deal that drains safe-haven demand.
Observed Attention: Reddit is betting on a $250 target for Oklo by July 4 even though the stock is down 24% Yahoo Finance [Feb 25].

Motivation & Bias: Policy extrapolation: Trump telling Big Tech to build its own power plants Reuters [Feb 25] is read as a direct bid for small reactors. The bias is to map a policy headline onto pre-revenue developers.

Instrument & Risk: Express nuclear demand through earnings-backed generators — CEG closed at 325.84 and VST at 175.36 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-25) — rather than pre-revenue reactor developers; if trading Oklo, use small option positions. Risk: one regulatory or financing delay can halve a pre-revenue stock.
